commits.message: style(test): wrap the busy plan literal and restore the import spacing (candybar-launch-q7o7.04z)

fix(render): a client timeout is a typed error that carries its phase (candybar-launch-q7o7.04z)

interpretException matched the message strings CONNECT_TIMEOUT and TIMEOUT, so a
reworded or wrapped error fell through to transient and kicked a live daemon.
ClientTimeoutError, thrown at both sites, carries the classification and the
phase (connect | deadline); BusyOutcome carries the phase too.

url-handle now exits 1 on a connect timeout, where the click was never written,
instead of exiting 0 and losing it behind a stderr line. A deadline, ours or the
daemon's own TIMEOUT, still exits 0: the click reached the daemon.

fix(render): a client timeout, on the connect or after it, kicks nothing (candybar-launch-q7o7.6wi) (#575)

* fix(render): a client timeout, on the connect or after it, kicks nothing (candybar-launch-q7o7.6wi)

A dead daemon never times out: a missing socket is ENOENT and an unbound one
ECONNREFUSED, both immediate. A timeout therefore means a live listener, and a
kick's candidate loses the bind to it (socket-lease arbitration). Both runtimes
now classify the client's own connect/deadline timeouts as busy, and the
unreachable-by-construction transient 'timeout' cause is removed.

* docs(render): busy comments say a daemon holds the socket, not that it answered (candybar-launch-q7o7.6wi)

* test(debug): a busy daemon is a stderr line with no spawn hint (candybar-launch-q7o7.6wi)

* docs(render): the busy and click-budget comments stop saying the daemon answered (candybar-launch-q7o7.6wi)

docs(design): the isolated daemon, tmux events and browser surface designs

Goals, architecture, contracts and one document per area, with the surveys and probes behind them. The Frame is recorded as built, and the browser surface is un-parked.
fix(bar-pane): a frame overwrites its rows and lands whole, so the pane stops flickering
